title: Educato vs Gizmo for studying from your own notes
summary: Choose Gizmo if creating and memorizing decks is the main job.
body_markdown:
Choose Gizmo if creating and memorizing decks is the main job. Choose Educato if the material also calls for explaining a process aloud and paid live voice fits your budget.

## Educato vs Gizmo: which should I use with my workshop notes?


Choose Gizmo for a deck of recall questions, or Educato when the exam asks you to explain a workflow from your notes. Look at the last question your instructor asked. If it was “Which two items go in the submission folder?” a Gizmo deck gives you a place to rehearse the list until you can produce it from memory. If it was “Would you accept this submission, and why?” you also need somewhere to try a whole answer. Educato supports AI-graded open answers and has a tutor, Plumi, for explanations. Here is how that difference plays out with one page of notes.


### Turn a workshop rule into three useful cards


Imagine a writing workshop with this rule on its handout. To submit a revised article, include a dated comment from a peer who read the draft. In a separate response log, identify one suggestion and explain what you changed or why you kept the original wording. The author may disagree with the reader. Both records go in the folder, even when the author accepts every suggestion. These are invented course instructions you can use as a practice exercise.


Take the role of the person checking folders. Maya submits a dated peer comment asking her to replace “nearby” with a walking distance. Her revised article now says “a ten-minute walk.” She mentions the edit at the workshop and puts the draft and comment in the folder. Would you accept it? Before reading on, name the smallest addition that would make the folder complete. Asking Maya to do the whole assignment again would miss something she already did.


A weak card asks “Did Maya forget her log?” You can get the right answer by agreeing with the question. A stronger card asks “Which document shows how the author handled a reader’s suggestion?” Put “the response log” on the back. For a second card, reverse the task: “What two things must a response log tell the checker?” The answer is the suggestion and the author’s action or reason for keeping the wording. Remembering the document’s name earns only the first card.


Use the third card to catch a plausible mistake. “A peer recommends a new headline. The author keeps the old one. What belongs in the log?” Accept an answer that identifies the recommendation and explains the decision. Reject “get a different peer to approve the headline.” The handout requires the author to consider a suggestion. It gives the peer no power to veto the final draft. Keep that last sentence on the back if you find yourself making that particular mistake.


### What an open answer reveals about the same folder


Return to Maya. “Incomplete because the author ignored feedback” gets the decision right for the wrong reason. The revised sentence actually shows that Maya followed the suggestion. A stronger answer reads, “The dated comment documents the peer review. Maya has already made the distance more precise. Add a response log entry identifying the request and the edit so a checker can trace the change.” You can defend each sentence by pointing to either the handout or an item in the folder.


To practice this in Educato, bring the workshop handout as a PDF or a photo of your written notes. Try an open answer with the folder closed. After reading the feedback, underline the words in your own answer that identify the missing record. Then circle the evidence you used to decide that the peer had done enough. If you can underline a document name but have nothing to circle, you have a specific sentence to work on next time.


Educato is best for this exercise when your sources are split across a handout, presentation and handwritten annotations and you want to explain a decision in your own words. Limits: full access is paid, and live voice requires a paid plan. If oral defense is part of the assignment, try explaining why a dated comment alone leaves the checker guessing. Someone preparing for a written quiz can do the same exercise on paper and put the two missed details back into a deck.


## Which Gizmo alternatives help me practice explaining an unfamiliar example?


Consider Educato when your cards have become easy but a fresh folder still gives you trouble. Change just one item in Maya’s submission. This time the folder contains a complete response log and a peer comment with no date. Which single correction would you request? If you immediately say “add the log,” the familiar story has become a cue. The correction is to date the comment. An explanation should acknowledge that the log already accounts for the edit.


If you struggle instead to remember what a checker must look for in the first place, keep the Gizmo deck. Give the cards short fronts you could answer without seeing Maya’s name. Separate the requirement about dating a comment from the requirement about explaining an edit. That way a missed card tells you exactly which detail needs another pass. Revisit the whole folder after you can retrieve both details with the backs covered.


## Is Gizmo worth it if I already have a deck?


Gizmo’s free plan allows unlimited cards and decks. Memorise uses up to 15 hearts, and Magic Import has a 20-minute wait between imports. For a workshop with one new handout a week, the wait may fall entirely between study sessions. For someone importing several sets of notes during a short break, that same interval can shape the whole session. Count how often the next import is actually ready to go while you are still waiting.[Read the product details](https://help.gizmo.ai/en/articles/15647627-what-do-i-get-with-gizmo-unlimited) .


Unlimited removes the heart and import-wait limits and includes unlimited AI Tutor and hints. Gizmo lists weekly and yearly options. Check the amount alongside the billing period in your own offer before choosing one. If the workshop deck fits comfortably in free practice, try the changed-folder question before buying more capacity. If you can explain both decisions and your recurring problem is an interrupted Memorise session, the paid feature addresses the difficulty you actually observed.
